articles.title: Job Offer Rescinded After Acceptance by Another Company
articles.summary: A woman's job offer was unexpectedly rescinded after she accepted another position.
articles.content: A woman's job offer was unexpectedly rescinded by a company after she had already accepted another position in preparation for her departure. The individual, Alexandra Plainte, 36, who resides near Sarasota, Florida, has shared her story of how this experience has altered her perspective on job security. Plainte's previous role as technical-support leader was not providing the growth opportunities she desired. She had been seeking a new challenge and found an opportunity as senior manager of technical support at another company. The interview process for the position was thorough, involving four rounds over two months with five participants, including the chief technology officer. The job search process was not taken lightly, as it directly impacted the family's financial situation. I was targeting senior manager and director positions at software companies, which indicated a desire for career advancement. The offer that came through seemed like the ideal next step in my professional journey. Accepting the role on the spot was a spontaneous decision, driven by the excitement of the opportunity. The position not only carried a senior title but also reported directly to the chief technology officer, suggesting significant growth prospects. Being part of the CTO's direct team was seen as a major plus, implying that I would have access to valuable mentorship and resources. This perception further fueled my enthusiasm for the role, which seemed too good to pass up. The formal offer letter from the company arrived shortly after the initial call with the recruiter. The document outlined the terms of employment, including salary details and benefits. In preparation for my new role, I submitted necessary paperwork, such as my background check and I-9 form. The recruiter informed me that due to organizational changes and budget realignment, they had eliminated the role and were rescinding the offer. This decision was unrelated to my performance during the interviews or the outcome of my background check. The news came as a shock, especially since I had already given notice at my previous job. My mind was racing with uncertainty about what this meant for my future. The recruiter reassured me that the decision was not personal and had nothing to do with my qualifications or fit for the role. However, the sudden change left me feeling devastated. I had shared the news of my new job with friends and family, and now I had to break the news to them that it wasn't happening after all. This added an extra layer of difficulty to an already stressful situation. I couldn't help but think about the what-ifs in this situation. With some savings set aside, I knew how hard the job market can be, especially when you're out of work for a long time. The thought of watching my financial cushion slowly disappear was daunting and scary. My recent purchase of an iPhone still felt like a luxury item, but it also served as a reminder that I had been looking forward to this new chapter in my career. When I checked the job posting at my previous company, I saw that over 700 people had applied for the role I was about to leave. This only reinforced my decision to focus on moving forward and explore other opportunities. Whether it's building something of my own or joining another software company, I'm determined to make the most of this unexpected turn of events. After being left in limbo by the company's decision to rescind their job offer, I've been focusing on creating multiple streams of income and building my professional network. This involves actively applying for new positions, while also exploring opportunities to start my own venture - a move that requires careful consideration and planning. By diversifying my options, I aim to minimize the risk associated with relying solely on a single job. Ultimately, it's become clear that having multiple irons in the fire is essential in today's unpredictable job market, where careers can change direction quickly. articles.title: Navigating Today's Competitive Job Market Requires More Than Just a Solid Resume and Cover Letter
articles.summary: A seasoned nonprofit CEO shares strategies to help her daughters stand out in today's job market.
articles.content: As a seasoned leader and nonprofit CEO, I've learned that navigating today's competitive job market requires more than just a solid resume and cover letter. With the rise of automation and artificial intelligence, employers are facing an overwhelming number of applications from qualified candidates. To help my daughters stand out in this crowded landscape, I've developed a set of strategies that emphasize personalized communication and tailored approaches. This includes crafting clear, concise application materials that demonstrate a deep understanding of the company's needs and values. My oldest daughter, Elizabeth, is a prime example of someone who has successfully navigated these challenges. With a master's degree from Emmanuel College and a math background from UMass Amherst, she landed a job handling security for the Red Sox. Her experience showcases the importance of having relevant skills and qualifications that align with the employer's requirements. In today's job market, it's essential to have a combination of technical expertise and soft skills that can be applied in a variety of contexts. As a nonprofit leader, I've seen firsthand how companies are seeking employees who not only possess specialized knowledge but also the ability to work collaboratively and think creatively. As a parent, it's not uncommon for me to draw on my own experiences when offering advice to my daughters. Both Lauren and Sarah have unique educational backgrounds - Lauren holds a degree in psychology from Northwestern University, while Sarah has an integrative education degree from Trinity College and a master's in social work from Case Western Reserve University. Given their diverse skill sets and interests, I encouraged them to explore various career paths. Currently, Elizabeth is employed as a video operations engineer at KISWE, while Sarah works as a business analyst for Education at Work, and Lauren is a consultant with both Echo Group and Edmentum. This exposure has helped me identify key areas where they can apply their skills. As I've been guiding them since elementary school, I've tried to instill in them the importance of being prepared for any opportunity that may arise. By accompanying me on business trips and observing my work habits at home - such as drafting RFP responses at the kitchen table late at night - they've gained valuable insight into the demands of a professional career. My advice to them has been to approach every situation with a mindset that views it as a potential opportunity for growth, even if it's not a formal interview. This includes showing up on time and being prepared for unexpected encounters, as these can sometimes lead to new connections or job openings. When attending online informational sessions, it's essential to make a good impression even in a virtual setting. Elizabeth's professionalism during such a session was noted by the host, who remembered her afterwards. This experience highlights the importance of being prepared and putting effort into each job application. When a position became available at MLB Replay, Elizabeth was selected from a pool of candidates on that same Zoom call, indicating that her preparation had paid off. To increase one's chances of getting noticed, it's crucial to personalize each job application using AI tools while still including specific details about relevant experience. This can be achieved by avoiding generic email copy and instead highlighting accomplishments that align with the job requirements. When applying online, look for opportunities to establish a warm connection, which can often lead to more attention than a cold email. Instead of sending emails to a generic inbox, try reaching out to a named person at the company, such as a recruiter, to establish a personal touch. When preparing for an interview, it's essential to identify the key areas you want to highlight about yourself and rehearse examples that demonstrate each of these strengths. This concept is often referred to as "win themes, where you showcase your skills and experiences in a way that resonates with potential employers. Incorporating transferable skills into this process can also be beneficial, allowing you to connect the dots between your past experiences and the role you're applying for. For instance, if you've volunteered at a sports program, you could explain how those skills are relevant to the work you want to do in a professional setting. Maintaining a journal dedicated to your career and profession can also be an effective way to track your progress and identify areas for improvement. By documenting both successes and setbacks, you can reflect on what went wrong and how you overcame challenges, thereby gaining valuable insights that will help you during the interview process. When reflecting on mistakes or difficult situations, consider turning them into opportunities to showcase your problem-solving skills. Ask yourself questions such as whether you could have handled a situation differently, whether you should have sought clarification, and what you can do in the future to avoid making similar errors. Applying for roles that seem beneath your level can be a valuable learning experience, even if it's not the perfect fit. It's essential to consider the job description rather than just the title when looking for opportunities. By doing so, you may discover skills and experiences that align with your goals. A memorable quote from an event in 1996 has stuck with me over the years: You will learn the most about the job and career you want from the job you hate." This phrase highlights the importance of understanding what you don't want to do as much as discovering what makes you happy. By exploring different roles, you can gain a deeper understanding of your strengths and weaknesses. Skills are not something that stop developing once you've entered the workforce; they continue to evolve throughout your career. One way to demonstrate growth is by asking for feedback and adjusting your approach based on it. Employers value professionals who incorporate feedback and use it as an opportunity to improve, showcasing their ability to learn from mistakes. When interviewing or networking, consider sharing examples of how you've incorporated feedback and improved over time. Additionally, ask thoughtful, personalized questions that demonstrate your genuine interest in the people and organization. This approach shows you've done your homework and are eager to learn more about potential future colleagues. When highlighting one's strengths, it's more effective to share specific anecdotes rather than making general statements. For instance, showcasing volunteer work or past experiences that demonstrate empathy and kindness can make a lasting impression on potential employers. This approach not only showcases skills but also provides tangible evidence of one's character. To prepare for video interviews, where nervousness might get the better of you, consider using visual reminders to stay focused. Placing sticky notes near the camera or taking a brief pause to grab a glass of water can help calm your nerves and ensure you don't go blank on screen. It's also essential to remember that it's okay not to be perfect, a genuine smile and deep breaths can work wonders in creating a more relaxed atmosphere. In-person interviews offer opportunities for creative preparation, such as bringing a neatly organized notebook with key points written down. This can help you stay on track without getting too caught up in your notes. However, it's crucial to remember that an interview is a conversation, not a formal presentation, try to build connections and avoid becoming overly reliant on your notes. articles.title: Migrant Girl Held at Shelter for Seven Months Pleads for Freedom
articles.summary: A young migrant girl has been held at a government-run shelter for over seven months, expressing desperation to leave and be reunited with her family.
articles.content: A young migrant girl held at a government-run shelter for over seven months has expressed her desperation to leave and be reunited with her family in the United States. Her words, scribbled on a piece of paper in misspelled Spanish, convey a sense of hopelessness and despair - "I love you surrounded by hearts, rainbows, and pink and blue dots is all that remains of her plea for freedom. According to an attorney representing the child, she had begged to be released from the shelter where she has been held captive for months. The attorney's account paints a picture of a helpless child crying out for help. The current administration's approach to migrant children appears to prioritize deportation over reunification with family members in the United States - a stark departure from previous policies aimed at prioritizing their well-being. The prolonged stay in shelters for migrant children has become a harsh reality, with many facing uncertain futures despite efforts to find suitable guardians. Attorneys report that the number of kids held in office shelters has decreased over the years, but those who remain are often stuck for months without a clear exit strategy, leaving them vulnerable to either long-term foster care or being sent back to their home countries. This situation arises when potential guardians get detained themselves, or are hesitant or unable to complete the sponsorship process due to various reasons. The Department of Homeland Security has responded to questions about detentions of migrant children's sponsors by pointing out that Immigration and Customs Enforcement is taking measures to prevent harm to the kids, framing these actions as part of their efforts. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) was sent questions by KFF Health News regarding a specific case involving an unaccompanied minor. The individual in question crossed the border with her older sister late last year, wading across the Rio Grande before being detained by Border Patrol officers in Texas. According to case documents, the sisters had hoped to join their mother and brother who had fled El Salvador a few years earlier and were living in Tennessee. Their father, uncle, and a pregnant cousin had also attempted to sponsor them, but Carmen, the girls' mother, feared for her daughter's safety due to these attempts. Before the second Trump administration took office, children typically waited about a month in the resettlement office's custody while federal officials screened their relatives or other sponsors. However, since then, the situation has changed significantly. The new requirements imposed by the administration have made it more difficult for sponsors to get children released from detention. Furthermore, parents and trusted caregivers who come forward to claim their children are now being arrested, adding to the complexity of the situation. The prolonged detention of migrant children in US shelters has led to devastating consequences for many young lives. A staggering 300 days is how long one 3-year-old child remained in custody, according to Alvaro Huerta from the Immigrant Defenders Law Center. Immigration lawyers have pointed out that the administration's actions have severely undermined legal protections for migrant children while simultaneously speeding up deportation procedures. As a result, many minors are being forced to appear before immigration judges without any representation, including some as young as 1 year old. In some disturbing cases, immigration officials are detaining kids who have already been placed with sponsors and are living in their communities. This has caused immense anxiety for families and communities that had welcomed these children into their fold. The complexity of the situation is further exacerbated by the fact that parents or trusted caregivers who come forward to claim their children are now being arrested, adding to the emotional trauma faced by these young individuals. The detention of a young girl has added to the emotional trauma faced by many migrant children stuck in shelters. The mother had been making progress towards reuniting with her child, having already submitted required documents and undergone a home visit from a social worker. The family's preparations for the reunion were evident, with the little girl's bedroom decorated with Hello Kitty bedding and Frozen" curtains. However, immigration officers detained the mother at an appointment without a warrant, leaving the child feeling lost and confused. According to Alexa Sendukas, managing attorney with the Galveston-Houston Immigrant Representation Project, the child is struggling to understand why her mom was detained instead of being reunited with her. The girl has received counseling at the Houston-area shelter where she is staying. The case highlights the difficulties faced by migrant families in navigating the complex reunification process. articles.content: Leaders from nearly a third of the world's population have converged on the Caribbean island of Antigua for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, a biennial gathering aimed at strengthening ties amidst global turmoil. The meeting, which takes place every two years, is expected to yield new deals and pledges as over 50 leaders from Commonwealth nations attend. These countries, many of which were once part of the British Empire, will be joined by officials from Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Brazil, and the United Arab Emirates. Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey has cautioned that the world is facing numerous challenges, including conflict, economic shocks, rising costs, climate change, trade disputes, and the weaponization of tariffs. These issues are having a direct impact on people's livelihoods, according to Botchwey. Botchwey emphasized that Commonwealth leaders representing 2.7 billion people will focus on attracting investment and reducing barriers to intra-Commonwealth trade during their meeting in Antigua. The gathering of Commonwealth leaders in Antigua is expected to focus on boosting economic resilience amidst global trade tensions. Botchwey emphasized that intra-Commonwealth trade can serve as a buffer against external shocks, allowing member countries to minimize their exposure to the fallout from trade wars. This concern is particularly relevant given the recent imposition of high import duties by U.S. President Donald Trump, which have been among the highest since the Great Depression, despite fluctuations due to ongoing legal challenges. In response to these trade tensions, the Commonwealth aims to create stronger economies through increased intra-regional trade and investment. The organization also seeks to provide digital skills training to approximately 10 million young adults through a new fund, with hopes that private sector contributions will be forthcoming. The upcoming Commonwealth forum in Antigua will also focus on addressing the needs of Indigenous populations, according to organizers. They aim to bring these communities into the conversation and explore ways to overcome the barriers they face. A key challenge for civil organizations is accessing financing, which often requires writing effective proposals. The forum is expected to propose initiatives that help address this issue, enabling more groups to secure funding. Climate change will also be a major topic of discussion at the meeting. The event's agenda includes discussions on slavery reparations, which some Caribbean leaders have requested be included in the four-day meeting's agenda. With King Charles III and Queen Camilla expected to attend, their presence will undoubtedly add weight to these conversations. The forum is set to conclude on Wednesday. articles.title: FBI Investigates Former Teacher Running for Senate Seat
articles.summary: The FBI has begun investigating Dan J. Sullivan, a former elementary school teacher running against Senator Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska's Senate election.
articles.content: In the small Alaskan fishing town of Petersburg, a sense of unease has settled over residents as news spreads that FBI agents have begun investigating Dan J. Sullivan, a former elementary school teacher who had been running a quixotic campaign to unseat Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan. The only indication that something out of the ordinary is happening lies in a small, non-partisan yard sign from the League of Women Voters, which reads "Stand Up for Democracy: Vote 2026". The investigation has taken on a serious tone as it appears to focus on allegations of "ballot stacking, a campaign tactic that could lead to criminal charges. This development comes after news emerged that the Trump administration is considering such charges in connection with Sullivan's campaign. Local residents, including those who donated to Sullivan's campaign, are expressing confusion and concern over the FBI's actions. Sharon Hunter, one such donor, spoke out about the investigation, saying she believes it represents a waste of taxpayer money and questioning the motives behind targeting someone who has been a positive force in the community. The tactics of Alaska's quirky politics have come under fresh scrutiny in the ongoing Senate election between incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola. The state's open primary and ranked choice voting systems make it easier for lesser-known candidates to play spoilers when no contender secures a majority. Sullivan has been fighting off a serious challenge from Peltola, who is seeking to distance herself from allegations of chicanery in the race. A recent New York Times article linked a group backing Peltola to a Democratic operative trying to recruit decoy candidates. Peltola's campaign has denied any involvement in such tactics, with the candidate telling supporters at a rally that This is Alaska. We're not in the business of tricking each other up here. Her statement reflects the unique dynamics of Alaska's politics, where cooperation and trust are often valued over cutthroat competition. As Sullivan navigates this challenging election, he has faced scrutiny since June, when the Alaska Division of Elections tried to remove him from the primary ballot. The move was sparked by concerns that Sullivan had not filed his candidacy as a Republican in good faith. The controversy surrounding Dan Sullivan's candidacy has taken a new turn as investigators from the FBI have begun making inquiries in the small fishing community of Petersburg. Local residents who know Sullivan personally are speaking out about his character and past work in the area. Several individuals described him as a creative teacher who ran an after-school program called Little Kids Rock to teach guitar skills to children. The program was well-received by students and parents alike, with many praising Sullivan's dedication to providing musical education opportunities. In fact, more than a dozen residents expressed admiration for Sullivan, calling him a valued member of the community. As investigators delve deeper into the matter, it remains unclear what specific actions or conversations will be scrutinized as part of the federal probe. The FBI's investigation into a Petersburg election scandal has taken a new turn, with authorities expanding their probe and descending on the small Alaskan town in recent days. The move has left locals feeling uneasy and wondering what specific actions or conversations will be scrutinized as part of the federal inquiry. In the tight-knit fishing community, residents have been sharing stories about Dan J. Sullivan's campaign, which received a significant amount of support from local donors. articles.title: Temporary Ceasefire Brings Respite to Residents Trapped in Ukraine's Kherson Region
articles.summary: A brief ceasefire has brought temporary respite to residents trapped in Ukraine's Kherson region, where the village of Kozatske is situated on the frontline between Ukrainian and Russian forces.
articles.content: A brief ceasefire has brought temporary respite to residents trapped in Ukraine's Kherson region, where the village of Kozatske is situated on the frontline between Ukrainian and Russian forces. The 53-year-old Nataliia Diadiuk lives in one of the few remaining homes in Kozatske, a riverside village less than two kilometers from Russian-controlled areas. With basic supplies scarce, she has resorted to gathering rainwater for drinking and firewood for heating her home. Diadiuk's daily life is marked by fear and uncertainty, as she navigates the dangers of living on the edge of a war zone. A white towel hung on her gate and a white rag held in her hand are her only means of signaling to Russian drone operators that she is a civilian, attempting to avoid being targeted. As the residents of Kozatske struggle to survive, Diadiuk longs for silence and the return of those who have fled. She wants to see her neighbors again, many of whom have been forced to leave due to the intense fighting in the area. The local residents' plight is further complicated by the presence of mines scattered throughout the village, making every step outside a perilous one. Despite these challenges, Diadiuk remains determined to stay in her home, even as she acknowledges the risks involved. A team from an international news organization has gained rare access to this so-called red zone, where they witnessed firsthand the dire conditions faced by those living in the kill zone of Ukraine's Kherson region. Civilians are trapped in various locations on both sides of the front line, mirroring the dire situation in Oleshky. Regional officials, police, and volunteers, facilitated by civil-military cooperation specialists, used the brief ceasefire to reach people cut off for nearly two years. A total of 180 people were evacuated from riverside communities and Kherson city, including 23 children, according to the regional administration. This leaves approximately 140,000 individuals still living in the Ukrainian-held part of the region. The pre-war population of this area was around 1 million residents. The region is now largely under Russian control, with nearly 70% of its territory seized by Russian forces. The riverside areas are designated as a red zone, signifying the highest level of military danger due to ongoing drone strikes and artillery bombardments. Residents will once again face these risks following the ceasefire's end. Abandoned cars sit on roadsides where they were hit, alongside destroyed ground robots that Ukrainians have attempted to deploy down treacherous routes. A lone reminder of peacetime still stands: a "Thank you for keeping the roadside clean" sign, now surrounded by devastation. Many houses in Diadiuk's village are reduced to charred walls, while glide bombs have created craters and shell fragments protrude from the asphalt like twisted metal flowers. Mines dropped from drones lie scattered throughout the area, some resembling intricate petals or wrapped in makeshift materials that require careful avoidance. The aftermath of war is evident in the overgrown ruins of empty houses, where vegetation has reclaimed what's left behind. This stark contrast highlights the harsh reality faced by those living in this conflict zone. As Diadiuk navigates the treacherous landscape of Kozatske, she's confronted by the haunting sounds of abandoned dogs howling in the distance. These canine companions have become an integral part of her daily life, and she struggles to leave them behind despite the danger. The prolonged siege has taken a toll on Diadiuk's sense of time, making it difficult for her to keep track of days. She only checks her phone occasionally to determine the current date, as charging the device is a laborious process that requires solar panels. To ensure access to safe drinking water, Diadiuk employs a makeshift filtration system. Rainwater is collected and strained through gauze before being treated with chlorine and boiled. Although the water quality has improved somewhat, the presence of dead bodies in nearby houses makes it difficult to fully trust its safety. The village's ordeal began shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion when Kozatske was occupied by Russian forces. Following Ukrainian liberation, the area gradually came under siege from drones as the conflict escalated into a more technological war. Resident Oleksii Shavokin has adapted to life in the besieged village by rationing his food and relying on old humanitarian aid for sustenance. He's managed to maintain a meager diet that consists of eggs from his remaining hens, which he carefully conserves to last as long as possible. Shavokin's home was damaged in an early 2023 mortar attack, but he's since repaired the structure and continues to reside there. His weight has significantly decreased due to the scarcity of food, dropping by approximately 30 kilograms from a pre-war total of nearly 100 kilograms. The dire situation in Kherson's riverside kill zone has left many residents torn between staying and fleeing for their lives. For those who choose to stay, the risk of being caught in crossfire or hit by a stray bullet is ever-present. Many of these residents are hesitant to leave because they fear that once they depart, they will be left without means to survive. Oleh Tarabaka, head of the Nova Kakhovka city military administration, explained that this is a common concern among those who have lived in Kherson their entire lives. They worry about losing their livelihoods and having no one to rely on. The fear of uncertainty and the unknown has taken hold of many residents' minds, making it difficult for them to make a decision about leaving or staying. Tarabaka noted that this is not just a matter of survival but also about the psychological toll of living in such conditions. Some residents are more willing to leave than others, often due to persuasion from military officials and evacuation groups. In some cases, family members have been able to convince their loved ones to make the decision to leave, as was the case with Yevhen and his mother Antonina. The temporary lull in fighting has provided a brief window of opportunity for evacuations to take place, but it remains unclear how long this reprieve will last. The situation on the ground remains precarious, and residents are holding their breaths as they wait to see what the future holds. The temporary ceasefire in Kherson city has provided a rare opportunity for residents to escape the dangers that have made their town a kill zone. The streets are eerily empty, save for the sounds of weeping and wailing from those who refuse to leave. Under normal circumstances, evacuation efforts are fraught with peril due to the constant threat of drones and other weapons. However, during the ceasefire week, the Red Cross was able to evacuate significantly more people than usual, taking advantage of the brief window of calm. Commander Mykola Taranenko of the Ukrainian Red Cross Society's rapid response team in the Kherson region emphasized the risks involved in evacuation efforts. "Right now, some streets and places in Kherson are a kill zone too," he said. It's simply impossible to slip through there without facing very high risk. The numbers tell a story of just how precarious the situation remains. Normally, the Red Cross evacuates around 10 people per week. But during the ceasefire week, they took out an astonishing 32 individuals, including elderly couples like Volodymyr and Kateryna Yakuba. As the couple prepares to leave their home behind, Kateryna expressed her gratitude for the temporary reprieve. "We need to get out before the cold sets in," she said, referring to the impending winter months. The Ukrainian forces' advance has forced Russian troops to retreat from some areas in Kherson, creating a brief window for civilians to escape. As temperatures drop, the urgency is growing for those trapped in the city's riverside kill zone, where fighting continues despite the ceasefire. The situation remains precarious, with both sides exchanging fire and civilians caught in the crossfire. articles.title: Collagen Supplements and Skin Health: A Review of the Evidence
articles.summary: Research suggests that oral collagen intake may not directly impact skin health as previously thought.
articles.content: A growing number of people are turning to collagen supplements in an effort to reduce wrinkles and maintain youthful skin. But do these products live up to their promises? As someone who has been studying the science of skin aging, I was eager to investigate. Collagen is a crucial protein found throughout our bodies, forming the framework that gives skin its strength and elasticity. It's often likened to a trampoline mat - strong yet flexible. But as we age, our skin produces less collagen, leading to sagging and wrinkles. This has led many to wonder if taking collagen supplements could be the answer. The idea behind collagen supplements is straightforward: by topping up declining levels of this essential protein, we can restore our skin's youthful appearance. However, research suggests that the relationship between oral collagen intake and skin health may not be as direct as previously thought. In fact, the body has a complex way of processing ingested collagen. When taken orally, collagen is broken down into its constituent amino acids during digestion, rather than being absorbed intact by the body. This raises questions about how effective these supplements can really be in promoting healthy skin aging - and whether they're worth the cost. The breakdown of collagen into smaller fragments is a key aspect of how our bodies process these supplements. When we ingest hydrolysed collagen, which contains individual chains of 40 or fewer amino acids, it's quickly broken down in our digestive systems into even smaller fragments consisting of just one to three amino acids. This fragmentation occurs not only with collagen supplements but also when we consume whole collagen in foods such as salmon skin and bone broth that contain gelatine. These tiny amino acid fragments are then added to the pool of amino acids derived from other protein-rich foods like meat, dairy, and legumes. The skin uses these amino acid building blocks to synthesize new collagen, but the efficiency of this process declines with age. This is according to James Varani, a pathologist at the University of Michigan who has extensively studied skin collagen. He notes that there's no difference between taking a collagen supplement and consuming a nutrient-rich food like a good steak. Varani's research suggests that the reason our skin loses collagen as we age isn't due to a lack of necessary ingredients but rather an inefficiency in the cellular machinery responsible for assembling these components into new collagen. The idea that taking collagen supplements can smooth away wrinkles is a notion that's been gaining traction in recent years. However, a closer look at the available research reveals that these claims might be overstated. Studies claiming to show significant reductions in wrinkle depth after taking collagen supplements often report tiny differences - mere fractions of a millimetre. These results may not translate into noticeable improvements in skin appearance. Dermatologist Anjali Mahto and biostatistician David Grimes have sounded the alarm on methodological concerns in existing studies. They point out that many of these studies are industry-funded or involve authors with commercial ties to collagen manufacturers, raising questions about selective reporting and bias. Their criticism is not without merit, given that an overwhelming proportion of research in this area has been funded by companies with a vested interest in the outcome. This can lead to overly optimistic conclusions being drawn from flawed data. Exercise, on the other hand, has been shown to have a more tangible impact on collagen production. Regular physical activity has been found to increase the expression of collagen genes, suggesting that incorporating exercise into one's routine may be a more effective way to support skin health than relying on supplements alone. Sun protection is crucial for maintaining healthy skin, as excessive exposure to ultraviolet radiation from the sun can lead to the breakdown of collagen. Dermatologists emphasize the importance of shielding the skin from harmful UV rays, which stimulate enzymes that degrade collagen. Tretinoin, a vitamin A derivative, has been shown to increase collagen levels since the 1990s. This prescription-strength treatment is often recommended by dermatologists for its ability to reduce wrinkles and improve skin texture. However, it can cause side effects such as dryness, redness, and peeling if not used carefully. Certain therapies that intentionally injure the skin in a controlled manner can also stimulate collagen production. These include laser treatments, microneedling, dermabrasion, and deep chemical peels. While these methods are effective at boosting collagen levels, they come with significant drawbacks, including redness, rawness, and blistering. A gene therapy originally developed for a rare genetic condition has shown promise in promoting collagen production. This treatment targets individuals with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a disorder characterized by extremely fragile skin and large, painful wounds. A new gene therapy has been approved for individuals with a rare genetic disorder that causes extremely fragile skin. This treatment introduces new collagen genes into the skin to boost collagen production and help repair damaged tissue. The US was the first country to approve this therapy in 2023, followed by the UK later this year. Researchers are now exploring whether a modified version of this gene therapy can reverse signs of aging in people with normal skin. When pressed for an explanation, Stevens stated that she was simply "where I landed after some introspection and writing. She emphasized her commitment to the Democratic Party, saying she is a proud Democrat who wants Democrats to win. Stevens also acknowledged that Abdul El-Sayed, Levin's opponent, has gained support from many other Democrats, but stopped short of providing further insight into what drove her decision to endorse him. Stevens emphasized that her endorsement decision was not influenced by any personal changes or developments. However, she did mention a specific factor that contributed to her shift in support: El-Sayed's alliance with left-wing streamer and commentator Hasan Piker. This strategic partnership has raised eyebrows among some Democrats, who may view it as too divisive for the party's interests.
